steps.text: Heat oil over medium-high in a large saucepan. Add onion; cook and stir until tender. Add beans, tomatoes, oregano, and garlic powder. Bring to a boil.
Stir in rice. Cover; reduce heat and simmer for 5 minutes. Remove from heat; let stand 5 minutes before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Quick Black Beans and Rice
raw_recipe.description: This easy rice and beans recipe is pretty straight forward. Brown rice, black beans, tomatoes, and some onion — in 15 minutes you have a hearty meal.
raw_recipe.name: Quick Black Beans and Rice

recipeInstructions.text: Heat oil over medium-high in a large saucepan. Add onion; cook and stir until tender. Add beans, tomatoes, oregano, and garlic powder. Bring to a boil.

review.reviewBody:
Not bad but made some additions, I used long grain brown rice, sauted the onion, garlic then added the rice, 1 cup chicken broth, tomatoes and simmered for 20 mins. Then added the other ingredients, including some green pepper and 2 tbsp of red chili flakes.
We enjoyed this with some chicken enchiladas.

As written, I was not a big fan. I don't really care all that much for instant rice and throwing it all in the same pot just made it an unpleasant texture. So I made a few changes the second time and really enjoyed this dish! First, I switched to long grain rice and cooked it separately. Meanwhile, I sauted onions and fresh minced garlic in some olive oil, then added the beans (I love beans, so I upped it to two cans), tomatoes and cooked rice and switched the oregano for some fresh basil. Oh so yummy!!!

I went vegetarian a couple years ago, and this was one of the first recipes I had come across soon after giving up meat. Since then, I've probably made this recipe a hundred times, it's THAT good. It didn't take very long before I put my own spin on it to make it taste a little more like an authentic Mexican recipe. Instead of a can of stewed tomatoes, I used a can of Ro*tel. I also added a little bit of corn. Also, instead of using the standard Italian oregano, I used Mexican oregano that I brought back with me from a trip to Arizona, and instead of one teaspoon of it, I used two. I added about a tablespoon of ground cumin. When the time came to stir in the rice, I also added about 1/4 cup of water. I simmered for about 7-9 minutes according to package directions. Before serving, I garnished it with a sprig of cilantro. I really wowed my family...they ALL loved it!

I never give anything 5 stars but my daughter ate this and actually loved it!! I’m shocked and extremely pleased! So instead of onions, I use the green onions (scallions) and only use the green parts. Anyway, sate that in avocado garlic oil and add the black beans and diced tomatoes, I also added Italian seasoning and a dash of cardamom cumin and coriander for the perfect flavor. Of course salt and pepper to taste, let cook together until beans are soft and tasty. Added to white rice! Yummy!

This was amazing. I love eating rice sometimes, it feels more filling and satisfying, and this is a healthy way to eat rice with protein and flavor. I sauted the onions and crushed garlic with olive oil. I smoothied two tomatoes in a blender and added to the mixture. The rice cooks faster than the beans, so soaking the beans an hour or so before would be good. I used dried beans. Added some chili cayenne pepper to up the spiciness. It was so good!

This is a great, simple dish, but like others have mentioned, I made a few tweaks to the recipe:

1) I used brown basmati rice (cooked it first),
2) I sauteed minced garlic with the onions (instead of garlic powder),
3) I added about a 1/4-1/2 cup of water,
4) I did not have any dried oregano, so I added some some dried cilantro and dried basil instead,
5) I added some cumin and also some cayenne for a bit of heat.

One of the easiest and healthiest dishes you can make and it tastes so good. The best part of a dish like this is how flexible it is.

As a bachelor with a small budget for food and not a lot of time to cook extravagant meals, this has become one of my favorite meals. The stewed tomatoes make this dish. Last night I tried putting my own spin on it along with the advice from other reviewers; I used 2 cans of beans, 2 cloves of fresh garlic to replace the powder, 1/2 tsp cumin, a pinch of chili powder, a bit of chicken broth (1 cup was too liquidy, I had to drain some) and I added about 1/4 cup frozen corn and a small can of green chiles. I also cooked the rice seperately and did not mix in with the rest until it was on my plate as I do with most rice dishes. It turned out really good, but if I use 2 cans of black means again I will also use 2 cans of stewed tomatoes and probably will sautee a jalepeno to give it some more kick. This is a truly guilt-free meal as it is cheap, healthy, and vegetarian along with being actually very delicious.

yumm! added a large minced garlic, added a cup and a half of juice left from slow cooker pork, a cup of water w/ chkn bullion cube and added 1/2 tsp onion powder. omitted tomatoes. used large silver pot, rice stuck on bottom (don't mix w/ rest of rice b/c it was a little hard... separate b/c it was delicious... had lots of flavor!)

I followed the recipe, except I added a can of Rotel canned tomatoes with seasonings (mild) instead of the canned tomatoes. I didn't use garlic powder, I used garlic in a jar (about a teaspoon). This is really easy to fix, especially since I'm cooking for one this week. I will reheat this for another meal, and toss in some baked chicken with a sprinkle of cheddar cheese after it's finished. Nice and hearty meal.

This recipe is a keeper! The only changes I made were, I used long grain brown rice that I cooked separate (adds to the time). I used minced garlic when cooking the onions instead of garlic powder. I also added chili powder and some kielbasa I had on hand.

Here's the thing - either use 1 cup of brown rice or add about 1/2 cup of water to the dish - the liquid isn't enough for the rice. Also might add some salt and pepper depending on the tomatoes you choose.
This was delicious! I will make it again.

I love quick and easy meals so I appreciated this one and will keep it. I used diced tomatoes with green chilies in tomato juice because that’s what I had. I believe that added some spiciness to it, but that was OK with me. Even though I let the rice have just a few more seconds in both steps because of the reviews it was still kind of chewy, but that’s easy to fix.

I've never made beans and rice before so I am not an expert but it seemed kind of bland to me. Also, I followed the recipe exactly. It said to cook the rice 5 minutes and let it sit 5 minutes. My instant brown rice box said to cook it 10 minutes. I should have followed the box directions because the rice was undercooked. Otherwise I was just o.k. to me.

Followed the recipes but added diced green peppers after cooking the onion as well as canned sweet corn. I had some non quick cook rice which I prepared separately before adding to the mic with a cup of chicken broth.

This was very good. Very few changes were made. I didn't have instant brown rice and didn't want to spend 45 minutes boiling regular brown rice, so I used cooked white rice. It was served with shrimp and a salad which made a great meal.

I made it for my family the rice was burnt and dry, it looked red, not black like in the photo. It probably would have been better if someone else made it 😕. My family took one bite, and we went out for food.
Loved it. Added some hot sauce. Green pepper would be good addition.

OK as a side for the Dijon Salmon. Quick and easy to prepare. If I had more time, I would have preferred a richer side, with basmati rice rather than instant, more interesting spices and maybe another ingredient. Good base for experimenting.

Seems a lot of recipes I see don't offer enough spices for my palate. I use the recipes as guidelines and then either add additional spices or use more of what the recipe calls for. Addition of chili powder is a good enhancement for this recipe.
